Right: a freight yard with a crane and plain unmarked containers, a roundhouse and turntable with steam locomotives, and a small unmanned halt with a platform shelter. Lower part of the picture: a river with a steel girder rail bridge and a road bridge, riverbank paths with strolling people and a photographer, fields, a road with cars, rows of trees and passing trains. About eight model trains (an express, a local train, freight trains, a steam train, a tram) run on the tracks. About 180 minuscule hand-painted figurines of people, each doing something: passengers, a station master, porters with luggage carts, people queueing at the kiosk, workers in the freight yard, hikers, farmers, strollers, children. A standing person is only about 3% of the picture height.

The look is the point: it must look like a real photograph of a handmade model railway: static-grass flocking, foam lichen trees, painted plaster hills and rock faces, ballasted track, plastic buildings with a slight sheen, tiny figurines with faces made of dabs of paint, soft studio lighting and a true tilt-shift miniature look: sharp in the middle band, with a gentle blur only in the top and bottom 12%. Not a real city, not a flat illustration, not a CG render. The picture fills the whole frame to all four edges: no table edge, no room, no hands, no frame, no border, no caption.

Exactly one small logo: a small black station name board on the little unmanned halt in the right half of the picture, about 4% of the picture width, with a white paw print whose big pad holds a swirling ocean wave, and the word "Shoji" in white cursive brush lettering to its right. Apart from that board there are no letters, words, numbers or digits anywhere: no station names, no destination boards, no timetables, no train numbers, no advertisements, no signs; the clock face has plain tick marks only.

THE ONLY ANIMALS IN THE WHOLE PICTURE ARE FOUR CATS, and there are never more than four. Not five, not a spare one, and no look-alike twin of any cat. No other animal at all: no cows, horses, sheep, ducks, birds, dogs or fish, no animal figurines or animal pictures. No person wears an animal head or costume. The four cats are tiny hand-painted model figurines like the people, all in the upper and middle part of the picture: their feet are between about 15% and 60% of the picture height measured from the top, and NONE is in the lower third (the lower third is only river, bridges, riverbank paths, fields, roads, trees and trains). Each cat is in the open, never hidden behind anything. The three real cats are each TINY: only about 0.7% of the picture height (about 14 pixels in a 2048-pixel-high picture), about a quarter of the height of a standing person, and wear a thin red collar with a tiny gold bell:
1. a black-and-white "hachiware" cat (black head and back, a white blaze splitting the face, white chest and paws) sitting upright on a platform bench of the central station, in the left half;
2. a brown mackerel tabby (warm brown fur with dark stripes, white muzzle and chest) sitting upright on a flat grey rock on the grassy hillside above the tunnel beside the mountain path, upper left;
3. a calico cat (white with orange and black patches) sitting upright in the doorway of the station kiosk with the striped awning, right of centre;
4. Shoji Cat, an upright standing orange tabby cat figurine about three heads tall in a black leather jacket, denim shorts, cream sneakers and black wayfarer sunglasses with blue and red lenses, standing in the crowd on the station plaza with one arm pointing, in the middle of the picture, about one and a half times as tall as each of the other three cats.
No dark round objects, no black tunnel mouths, no piles of black cloth or coal, and no dark animal-like shapes that could be mistaken for a cat. No watermark.

后 4 格讲参考图之后造成的结果，关键词：【后果关键词，2–3 个】
情绪走向：【例：平静→察觉→紧张→爆发→愣住→扩散→接受→释然】

4 前情·临界：特写，直接引发第 5 格那一刻的动作。

posts.text:
GPT image 2.5

Prompt:
Create a beautiful, vintage-inspired hand-drawn architectural illustration of [LANDMARK], [CITY], [COUNTRY], inspired by the charm of old travel sketchbooks and traditional pen-and-ink drawings.

Composition: Feature the most iconic landmark of [CITY] as the main subject, surrounded by authentic local architecture, historic buildings, charming streets, traditional transportation, vintage street signs, overhead wires, and small cultural details that make the place instantly recognizable. Include a tram, bicycle, old car, or other local transportation where appropriate.

Art Style: Use delicate black ink linework, expressive hand-drawn strokes, intricate architectural details, fine cross-hatching, imperfect outlines, and an unfinished sketchbook aesthetic. Keep the illustration predominantly monochrome on a clean, warm ivory-white background. Preserve the landmark’s authentic architecture, proportions, and recognizable features.

Typography & Title Design: Make the name of the place the visual highlight of the composition. Add [CITY, COUNTRY] in a beautiful, eye-catching vintage editorial font, such as elegant retro serif lettering, artistic hand-lettered calligraphy, or bold old-world typography. Give the lettering a distinctive personality, with graceful curves, carefully spaced characters, and a timeless travel-poster aesthetic.

Position the title harmoniously at the top or bottom of the illustration, ensuring it is clearly readable and beautifully integrated into the artwork. Make the city name prominent and the country name slightly smaller beneath it. Add subtle decorative flourishes, delicate ink ornaments, or thin vintage borders around the typography. The lettering should feel like a carefully designed title on a collectible travel poster, not ordinary computer text.

Historical Tagline: Beneath the place name, include a short, poetic line that reflects the destination’s history and character, such as:

“Every street remembers. Every stone tells a story.”

Generate a suitable, location-specific tagline for each destination.

Overall Atmosphere: Nostalgic, artistic, authentic, culturally rich, elegant, and timeless. The result should resemble an original illustration from a vintage travel journal, beautifully transformed into a collectible art print.

Color Palette: Primarily black ink on warm ivory paper, with subtle natural paper texture. Keep the composition minimal, airy, and sophisticated.

Avoid: Photorealism, 3D rendering, glossy digital effects, excessive colors, generic architecture, cluttered composition, and plain or poorly rendered typography.

Format: 4:5 portrait composition, high-resolution illustration, balanced negative space, professional editorial layout.

Replace these details for every new artwork:

Landmark: [LANDMARK]
City: [CITY]
Country: [COUNTRY]

The final result should feel like a beautiful vintage illustration with a memorable title—an artwork people would want to save, frame, and collect.

GPT image 2.5

PROMPT: 
THE WORLD IN WATERCOLOR — Where Photography Becomes Art

Create an extraordinarily beautiful luxury travel artwork featuring [CITY / COUNTRY / LANDMARK / NATURAL DESTINATION], combining breathtaking photorealistic landscape photography with delicate, flowing watercolour painting.

1. Overall composition

Create a sophisticated horizontal split composition in a vertical 4:5 or 2:3 art-print format.

LEFT HALF — THE WORLD AS IT IS

Show a breathtaking, photorealistic photograph of the destination.

* Capture its most recognizable natural landscape or architectural landmark.
* Include authentic surroundings, local vegetation and geographical details.
* Use beautiful natural daylight, realistic reflections and atmospheric depth.
* Preserve genuine colours, textures and architectural details.
* Create a professional luxury travel-photography aesthetic.

RIGHT HALF — THE WORLD IN WATERCOLOR

Transform the exact same scene into a beautiful flowing watercolour painting.

* Recreate the same mountain peaks, architecture, forests, lake or landscape.
* Use delicate transparent watercolour washes.
* Allow pigments to flow naturally beyond the edges of the scene.
* Incorporate soft colour bleeding, organic brushstrokes and layered pigments.
* Create beautiful watercolour textures on warm ivory handmade paper.
* Allow parts of the landscape to dissolve gently into abstract washes.
* Preserve the recognizable silhouette of the original destination.

2. The magical transition

Create a delicate vertical transition between photography and watercolour.

The landscape should appear to gradually transform from a real photograph into a hand-painted masterpiece.

Allow trees, mountain peaks, reflections and architectural details to continue naturally across both halves.

Avoid an overly rigid dividing line. Use flowing pigments and subtle paper textures to create an organic transition.

3. Destination identity — THE UNIQUE SIGNATURE

IMPORTANT: Include 2–4 authentic elements that make the selected destination instantly recognizable beyond its main landmark.

Automatically select culturally and geographically relevant detail
Integrate these elements naturally into the composition rather than adding them as unrelated decorations.

4. Flowing watercolour palette

Select a unique destination-inspired palette for every artwork.

Use soft, transparent pigments, subtle colour gradients and naturally blending tones.

The watercolour side should feel light, dreamy, atmospheric and beautifully expressive.

5. Typography and destination name

Add the destination name in elegant, refined uppercase typography near the bottom.

[DESTINATION NAME]

Below it, include a poetic, original tagline inspired by the place.

6. Artistic direction

Luxury travel photography, flowing watercolour illustration, handmade cotton paper texture, organic pigment blooms, delicate brushwork, atmospheric landscapes, sophisticated editorial composition and fine-art gallery aesthetics.

7. Final presentation

Premium collectible travel-art poster, vertical 2:3 composition, photorealistic and watercolour split, elegant typography, authentic destination details and exceptional artistic craftsmanship.

Use a clean white background, thin grid lines, and small readable numbers 1–16 in the upper-left corner of each panel. One full-body depiction of the character per panel, consistent scale, camera distance, lighting, and rendering style throughout. Fixed camera angle while the character turns naturally. UPPER HALF — ORIGINAL PHOTOGRAPH
Preserve the original landmark photograph as faithfully as possible. Maintain the landmark’s authentic architectural identity, silhouette, proportions, distinctive structures, windows, arches, columns, rooflines, materials, and characteristic colors. Retain the original lighting, natural shadows, surface textures, perspective, and surrounding environment.
Apply subtle art-magazine color grading with refined tonal contrast, sophisticated color balance, and a contemporary fine-art photography aesthetic. If necessary, extend the background naturally to achieve the portrait composition without stretching, distorting, replacing, or altering the landmark. The photograph should feel authentic, timeless, and editorial rather than artificially enhanced.
LOWER HALF — GEOMETRIC ARCHITECTURAL ABSTRACTION
Reinterpret the same landmark as a sophisticated modular geometric illustration. Translate its most recognizable architectural features into bold, simplified geometric structures while maintaining an unmistakable visual connection to the photograph above.
Construct the illustration using large rectangles, squares, rounded squares, circles, triangles, arches, and carefully composed irregular geometric forms. Recreate the landmark’s distinctive silhouette, structural rhythm, architectural proportions, and recognizable details through overlapping blocks, layered planes, simplified facades, and carefully balanced shapes.
Avoid excessive fragmentation, tiny geometric pieces, photorealistic rendering, and generic architectural symbols. Favor fewer, larger, cohesive forms with deliberate spacing and strong compositional structure. Preserve the landmark’s unique identity rather than turning it into an interchangeable building.
COLOR AND MATERIAL LANGUAGE
Develop the illustration’s palette from the original photograph and the visual character of [COUNTRY]. Use a restrained, harmonious combination of architectural neutrals, muted heritage tones, earthy pigments, and carefully selected accent colors.
Introduce subtle paper grain, matte printed surfaces, delicate screen-print textures, and refined color overlays. Maintain a sophisticated balance between flat geometric shapes and tactile printed materials.
EDITORIAL ART DIRECTION
Create the visual quality of a collectible architecture-art exhibition poster designed for a prestigious independent art magazine. Emphasize architectural rhythm, negative space, geometric balance, precise alignment, and visual continuity between the photographic and illustrated halves.
The upper photograph and lower illustration must depict the same landmark from a consistent visual perspective wherever possible. Align major contours, dominant verticals, recognizable towers, rooflines, or other signature features across the central division to strengthen the relationship between the two halves.
The result should feel artistic, architectural, culturally distinctive, contemporary, and suitable for a high-quality art print.
STRICT RESTRICTIONS
No text, typography, letters, words, numbers, captions, slogans, logos, watermarks, signatures, labels, borders, or graphic lettering anywhere in the image. Do not add flags, decorative national symbols, or unrelated landmarks unless they are present in the original photograph. Do not modify the landmark’s authentic identity. Do not merge multiple photographs. Produce one complete, independent poster from the supplied photograph.

Setting: A cozy bedroom with an off-white textured wall, soft white bedding, and a simple neutral background. Warm indoor lighting and consistent flash shadows across all six frames.

Outfit & Accessories: The same fitted burgundy long-sleeve scoop-neck top in every photograph, paired with small gold hoop earrings and a delicate gold pendant necklace. Natural makeup, softly flushed cheeks, subtle eyeliner, glossy lips, and loose, slightly tousled hair. Keep the neckline tasteful and moderately covered.

Six Different Poses:

2. Playful wink: Leaning slightly toward the camera, winking with puckered lips and a relaxed shoulder posture.
3. Over-the-shoulder glance: Turning her body away while looking back toward the camera, with long hair flowing down her back and a subtle confident expression.
4. Eyes-closed smile: One arm lifted behind her head, eyes gently closed, smiling peacefully while her hair falls naturally over her shoulders.

Avoid excessive retouching, plastic-looking skin, duplicated expressions, malformed fingers, distorted anatomy, artificial beauty filters, or overly polished AI-generated results.

[CITY NAME]

[COUNTRY NAME]

Typography should be perfectly aligned and visually balanced.

Use a warm ivory, pale cream or soft beige background with a very subtle paper texture.

Scandinavian minimalist illustration, architectural blueprint aesthetics, delicate black-line drawing, modern editorial poster design, geometric simplicity, refined typography and contemporary gallery art.

A sophisticated, timeless collectible architectural travel poster.

Strong visual hierarchy, generous negative space, accurate landmark silhouettes, delicate linework and beautifully balanced proportions.

プロンプト：GPT Image 2.5

A handmade layered paper-cut diorama (a "shadow box" of cut paper), horizontal 3:2, a "find the hidden cats" picture in the spirit of a classic seek-and-find book: a moonlit forest village by a river seen from far away in a pulled-back wide view, so that the picture holds a huge amount of tiny detail. It is built from EIGHT clearly separate sheets of paper stacked one behind the other, each a different flat color of real paper with visible fibre, crisp hand-cut edges and a soft cast shadow on the sheet behind it. From the front to the back: a thin dark indigo foreground sheet of curling branches along the top corners and bottom edge, a deep navy sheet of slender pine trunks, a teal sheet of the near forest, reeds and the riverbank, a plum-purple sheet with the village (many houses climbing terraced slopes, small arched stone bridges, a tea stall and a market square), a dusty-blue sheet of more houses and trees, a lavender sheet of rolling hills with a winding road, a pale peach sheet of distant mountains, and the back sheet: a small full cream moon in a pale gold sky. Warm amber and honey-yellow light leaks through the gaps and cut-out holes between the sheets, as if a lamp were hidden behind the diorama: windows, lanterns and the moon are cut-outs backed with glowing yellow tissue paper. A limited palette of indigo, navy, teal, plum, dusty blue, lavender, peach and cream, with the warm amber glow as the only bright accent. It must read as cut paper. The paper fills the whole picture to all four edges: no frame, no border.

About 200 tiny paper villagers in plain everyday clothes, each with a small story (an adult is only about 45 pixels tall in a 1360-pixel-high picture): a lantern parade of children, ferrymen poling small flat boats, a night market with plain striped awnings, a puppet show, a storyteller with listeners, women hanging lanterns on ladders, a boy on a swing, friends crossing arched bridges, a clock tower, a kite flyer, a juggler. Dozens of small cottages, a treehouse with lit windows, a windmill, a pagoda-like tower, stepping stones and reeds.

A logo appears exactly ONCE, small: a modest dark wooden signboard hanging at the front of the tea stall in the middle of the picture (about 4% of the picture width), showing a cream-colored cat paw print whose big pad contains a swirling ocean-wave shape, with the word "Shoji" in cream cursive brush lettering to its right. Apart from that logo there are NO letters, NO words, NO numbers anywhere.

Exactly FOUR cats are hidden in the scene and NO other animal: no birds, no insects, no fish, no dogs, no cat ears or masks on anybody, no cat painted on any sign. All four are on the same plum village sheet, in the open, easy to overlook, and ALL FOUR ARE THE SAME TINY SIZE: each about 1.4% of the picture height (roughly 20 to 25 pixels tall), about two fifths of an adult villager's height, no cat bigger than another:
(1) a black-and-white "hachiware" cat (black head and back, a white blaze splitting the face, white chest and paws) sitting upright on the ridge of a small cottage roof at the far left;
(2) a brown mackerel tabby (warm brown fur with dark stripes, white muzzle) sitting upright on a pine branch, center-left;
(3) a calico cat (mostly white with distinct orange and black patches) sitting upright on the stone rim of the village well beside the tea stall, center-right;
(4) an upright standing orange tabby cat about three heads tall, exactly as tall as the other three cats and as small as they are, far smaller than the villagers around him, wearing black wayfarer sunglasses whose lenses are blue on one side and red on the other, an open black leather biker jacket, rolled-up denim shorts and cream sneakers, pointing with one hand, standing on the top of an arched stone bridge at the right.
The tabby, hachiware and calico are real four-legged cats with a thin red collar and a tiny gold bell, no clothes. No cat appears in the lower third of the picture. No black or dark round object that could be mistaken for a cat. No watermark.

High-end underground fashion magazine editorial, experimental street fashion, avant-garde styling, cinematic urban photography, rebellious luxury aesthetic, raw fashion campaign, analog film-inspired texture, photorealistic skin details, realistic fabric rendering, sophisticated color grading, and dramatic atmospheric depth.

答えは一番下の返信に👇

posts.prompt:
答え合わせ🐈
赤い丸の中に4匹います。
・ハチワレ：左の切符売り場、窓口のカウンターの縁
・茶トラ：その右の輪投げ屋、景品棚の上
・Shoji Cat：観覧車のわきの通路で、手を上げて踊っています
・三毛：右のバンパーカー乗り場、行列の足元の地面
Shojiの看板は、右の風船屋です。

———

プロンプト：GPT Image 2.5

A huge hand-made felt-and-embroidery appliqué panel, horizontal 3:2, a "find the hidden cats" picture in the spirit of a classic seek-and-find book: a busy amusement park seen from a high, wide bird's-eye view so that everything is small and there is a huge amount to look at. In the middle a big Ferris wheel with colorful gondolas; on the left a spinning teacup ride, a small toy train and a pond with round pedal boats; on the right a bumper-car rink with a queue, a roller coaster looping in the background and tethered hot-air balloons. A paved plaza runs through the middle, and a small parade is under way on it: about fifteen people dancing and marching behind a decorated float, with streamers and flags. Along both sides stand small stalls with scalloped awnings: a ticket booth with a counter window, a ring-toss stall with a prize shelf, popcorn, cotton candy, ice cream, a balloon seller, a pretzel stand, a shooting gallery. Behind them round trees, flower beds and a dusk-blue sky with stars. In front, a crowd of about 150 tiny felt-doll people, each doing something (kids with balloons, a child on a father's shoulders, a vendor scooping popcorn, a photographer, a drummer in the parade). A standing person is only about 3% of the picture height, every figure tiny and crisp with a stitched face.

The look is the point: every shape is a cut piece of colored wool felt sewn onto a quilted cotton ground with visible blanket stitches, running stitches, satin-stitch fills and French knots, fuzzy fibres, little sequins and beads for the lights; warm cheerful palette of candy red, teal, mustard, blush pink, cream, leaf green and deep dusk blue. Seen flat from straight on in soft even light, like a photograph of a handmade textile artwork, not a digital painting or 3D render. Full bleed, no hoop, no frame, no border.

Exactly one small logo: a small dark navy felt signboard hanging at the front of the balloon seller's stall in the right half, about 5% of the picture width, with a cream-thread embroidered cat paw print whose big pad holds a swirling ocean wave, and the word "Shoji" in cream cursive brush lettering to its right. Apart from that sign there are no letters, words or numbers anywhere.

Exactly four cats are hidden in the scene and no other cat or animal anywhere (no fish, birds, rabbits, horses, plush animals, animal rides, mascots, masks or cat ears). The cats are all tiny, in the same band of the picture at the same distance, each in the open, never hidden behind anything, none in the lower third; the three real cats are each only about 1.5% of the picture height, about two fifths of a standing person, and wear a thin red collar with a tiny gold bell:
1. a black-and-white "hachiware" cat (black head and back, a white blaze splitting the face, white chest and paws) sitting upright on the counter ledge of the ticket-booth window on the left, next to the attendant;
2. a brown mackerel tabby (warm brown fur with dark stripes, white muzzle and chest) sitting upright on the prize shelf of the ring-toss stall, between star, heart and ball prizes;
3. a calico cat (white with orange and black patches) sitting on the pavement at the edge of the bumper-car queue, among the legs of the waiting people;
4. Shoji Cat, an upright orange tabby cat about three heads tall in a black leather jacket, denim shorts, cream sneakers and black wayfarer sunglasses with blue and red lenses, dancing with one arm raised on the path beside the Ferris wheel, a little taller than the other three cats.
No dark round objects or dark animal-like shapes that could be mistaken for a cat. No watermark.

Prompt: Task: Strictly edit the uploaded original photograph to transform the person or animal into a hyper-realistic, extremely exaggerated big-head miniature figure, matching the visual style of the provided reference image.

Highest Priority: Transform the head-to-body proportions while preserving the subject's recognizable identity, natural facial features, original expression, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, pose, and overall photographic realism. The final result must resemble a real photograph, not a cartoon or CGI creation.

1. Head-to-Body Proportions (Highest Priority)

- Giant Head: Dramatically enlarge the entire head, including hair, hats, ears, and other existing head accessories. The head should dominate the figure, occupying approximately 65–75% of the total visible silhouette height in a full-body composition.
- Extremely Narrow Shoulders: Reduce shoulder width to approximately 40–50% of the head width. Create a tiny neck and narrow shoulder structure that transitions naturally into the miniature torso.
- Miniature Body: Compress the torso, waist, hips, and limbs into an extremely small body beneath the oversized head. The torso should be short and narrow, with realistic anatomical connections.
- Miniature Arms and Hands: Reduce the arms, palms, and fingers proportionally. Keep the arms naturally close to the body, preserving the original gestures and hand positions.
- Tiny Legs and Feet: Dramatically shorten and narrow the legs, feet, and shoes while preserving the original stance, footwear design, and points of contact with the ground.
- Strong Proportional Contrast: The head must be unmistakably oversized relative to the tiny body. Preserve the subject's original clothing design while naturally adapting its fit to the miniature proportions.

The transformation must create an extreme, visually striking big-head miniature effect without making the subject look like a toy, doll, or digitally assembled figure.

2. Pose and Actions (Strictly Preserve)

Preserve the original subject's exact pose, body orientation, gestures, facial expression, gaze direction, and interactions with the environment.

- If standing, keep the subject standing in the same position.
- If sitting, crouching, leaning, kneeling, or lying down, preserve that exact posture.
- Retain the original hand positions, held objects, arm placement, leg orientation, and contact points.
- Maintain the original head tilt and gaze direction unless a slight anatomical adjustment is necessary for a seamless transformation.
- Keep the subject's original framing. For full-body photographs, preserve the entire figure. For selfies, close-ups, and partial-body images, do not invent missing body parts or expand the frame unnecessarily.

The miniature body must adapt to the original pose rather than forcing the subject into a new pose.

3. Facial Features, Hair, and Clothing (Fully Preserve)

- Identity: Preserve the same recognizable person or animal from the original image. Do not replace, reinterpret, or redesign the subject.
- Face: Retain the original facial structure, eye shape, nose, lips, cheeks, skin tone, expression, and natural facial proportions. Do not apply beauty filters, artificial eye enlargement, face reshaping, or excessive skin smoothing.
- Hair: Preserve the original hairstyle, hair color, hairline, texture, volume, and distinctive strands. Scale the hair naturally with the enlarged head.
- Clothing: Preserve the exact original garments, colors, materials, prints, patterns, logos, folds, and textures. Adapt their dimensions to fit the miniature body without changing their design.
- Accessories: Retain all original jewelry, glasses, hats, bags, watches, and other visible accessories, resizing them only when necessary to fit the transformed proportions.
- Animals: Preserve the original species, recognizable features, fur patterns, ears, eyes, and expression. Apply the same oversized-head and miniature-body transformation without changing the animal's identity.

4. Scene and Composition (Fully Preserve)

Use the uploaded photograph as the sole reference for the subject and environment.

- Preserve the original background, architecture, furniture, plants, ground surface, and environmental objects.
- Maintain the original camera angle, perspective, framing, subject placement, composition, and aspect ratio.
- Keep the surrounding environment at its original scale. The subject's altered proportions should create a striking contrast with the realistic environment.
- Preserve the original lighting direction, color tones, shadows, reflections, and depth of field.
- Ensure the miniature figure remains naturally grounded in the scene, with realistic contact shadows beneath the feet and physically consistent lighting across the enlarged head and reduced body.
- Do not remove, replace, or introduce environmental elements unless a minor reconstruction is essential to repair an editing artifact.

5. Photographic Realism and Visual Quality

The entire image must retain the appearance of an authentic, high-resolution photograph.

- Realistic skin pores, fine facial details, and natural skin texture.
- Individual hair strands with believable highlights and shadows.
- Authentic fabric weave, clothing folds, and accessory details.
- Natural lighting, physically accurate shadows, and consistent reflections.
- Seamless transitions between the enlarged head, neck, and miniature body.
- Realistic anatomy, natural edges, and coherent perspective.
- Subtle photographic imperfections consistent with the original image.

The oversized head must remain fully photorealistic, with the original person's natural facial anatomy and expression intact. The miniature body must look like a physically plausible part of the same person.

6. Strictly Prohibited

- Cartoon, anime, illustration, or stylized 3D figurine aesthetics.
- Plastic skin, toy-like materials, doll faces, or artificial beauty enhancements.
- Changing the subject's identity, facial features, expression, hairstyle, or clothing design.
- Normal adult shoulder width or a body that appears too large relative to the head.
- Oversized hands, fingers, feet, or shoes.
- Disconnected heads, visible neck seams, floating limbs, malformed joints, or duplicated body parts.
- Altered poses, invented gestures, or changed interactions with the environment.
- Unnecessary background replacement, camera-angle changes, or aspect-ratio changes.
- Unnatural shadows, inconsistent lighting, visible compositing artifacts, text, watermarks, or interface elements.

Final Output

Transform the original photograph into an ultra-photorealistic big-head miniature portrait with a dramatically enlarged head, extremely narrow shoulders, a tiny compressed body, and proportionally miniature limbs.

Preserve the original subject's identity, expression, pose, clothing, accessories, background, and photographic characteristics as faithfully as possible. The exaggerated head-to-body ratio should be the defining visual transformation, producing the same realistic, charming, oversized-head aesthetic as the reference image.

Editing Rule: Change the subject's proportions only. Preserve everything else from the original photograph.

2. Pose and Actions (Strictly Preserve)

Preserve the original subject's exact pose, body orientation, gestures, facial expression, gaze direction, and interactions with the environment.

- If standing, keep the subject standing in the same position.
- If sitting, crouching, leaning, kneeling, or lying down, preserve that exact posture.
- Retain the original hand positions, held objects, arm placement, leg orientation, and contact points.
- Maintain the original head tilt and gaze direction unless a slight anatomical adjustment is necessary for a seamless transformation.
- Keep the subject's original framing. For full-body photographs, preserve the entire figure. For selfies, close-ups, and partial-body images, do not invent missing body parts or expand the frame unnecessarily.

The miniature body must adapt to the original pose rather than forcing the subject into a new pose.

3. Facial Features, Hair, and Clothing (Fully Preserve)

- Identity: Preserve the same recognizable person or animal from the original image. Do not replace, reinterpret, or redesign the subject.
- Face: Retain the original facial structure, eye shape, nose, lips, cheeks, skin tone, expression, and natural facial proportions. Do not apply beauty filters, artificial eye enlargement, face reshaping, or excessive skin smoothing.
- Hair: Preserve the original hairstyle, hair color, hairline, texture, volume, and distinctive strands. Scale the hair naturally with the enlarged head.
- Clothing: Preserve the exact original garments, colors, materials, prints, patterns, logos, folds, and textures. Adapt their dimensions to fit the miniature body without changing their design.
- Accessories: Retain all original jewelry, glasses, hats, bags, watches, and other visible accessories, resizing them only when necessary to fit the transformed proportions.
- Animals: Preserve the original species, recognizable features, fur patterns, ears, eyes, and expression. Apply the same oversized-head and miniature-body transformation without changing the animal's identity.

4. Scene and Composition (Fully Preserve)

Use the uploaded photograph as the sole reference for the subject and environment.

- Preserve the original background, architecture, furniture, plants, ground surface, and environmental objects.
- Maintain the original camera angle, perspective, framing, subject placement, composition, and aspect ratio.
- Keep the surrounding environment at its original scale. The subject's altered proportions should create a striking contrast with the realistic environment.
- Preserve the original lighting direction, color tones, shadows, reflections, and depth of field.
- Ensure the miniature figure remains naturally grounded in the scene, with realistic contact shadows beneath the feet and physically consistent lighting across the enlarged head and reduced body.
- Do not remove, replace, or introduce environmental elements unless a minor reconstruction is essential to repair an editing artifact.

5. Photographic Realism and Visual Quality

The entire image must retain the appearance of an authentic, high-resolution photograph.

- Realistic skin pores, fine facial details, and natural skin texture.
- Individual hair strands with believable highlights and shadows.
- Authentic fabric weave, clothing folds, and accessory details.
- Natural lighting, physically accurate shadows, and consistent reflections.
- Seamless transitions between the enlarged head, neck, and miniature body.
- Realistic anatomy, natural edges, and coherent perspective.
- Subtle photographic imperfections consistent with the original image.

The oversized head must remain fully photorealistic, with the original person's natural facial anatomy and expression intact. The miniature body must look like a physically plausible part of the same person.

6. Strictly Prohibited

- Cartoon, anime, illustration, or stylized 3D figurine aesthetics.
- Plastic skin, toy-like materials, doll faces, or artificial beauty enhancements.
- Changing the subject's identity, facial features, expression, hairstyle, or clothing design.
- Normal adult shoulder width or a body that appears too large relative to the head.
- Oversized hands, fingers, feet, or shoes.
- Disconnected heads, visible neck seams, floating limbs, malformed joints, or duplicated body parts.
- Altered poses, invented gestures, or changed interactions with the environment.
- Unnecessary background replacement, camera-angle changes, or aspect-ratio changes.
- Unnatural shadows, inconsistent lighting, visible compositing artifacts, text, watermarks, or interface elements.

Transform the original photograph into an ultra-photorealistic big-head miniature portrait with a dramatically enlarged head, extremely narrow shoulders, a tiny compressed body, and proportionally miniature limbs.

Preserve the original subject's identity, expression, pose, clothing, accessories, background, and photographic characteristics as faithfully as possible. The exaggerated head-to-body ratio should be the defining visual transformation, producing the same realistic, charming, oversized-head aesthetic as the reference image.

Editing Rule: Change the subject's proportions only. Preserve everything else from the original photograph.

Prompt:
Create a premium 4:5 vertical travel-editorial artwork for [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT].

PURE GENERATION.
Invent the complete artwork from the written destination or subject alone. The written destination is the only input. Create every visual element from your own knowledge and imagination.

MASTER STYLE LOCK:
Hand-painted watercolor on warm cream textured paper. Minimalist travel-editorial poster. Transparent watercolor blended with soft gouache. Soft imperfect brushwork, visible paper grain, organic painted edges, muted natural colors, generous negative space, quiet nostalgic atmosphere, sophisticated handcrafted art-book quality. Flat illustrated artwork with painterly depth. No 3D rendering, no glossy finish, no cartoon style, no digital photorealism.

DESTINATION INTERPRETATION:
Automatically identify the strongest visual identity of [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT]. Select the most recognizable landmark, architecture, landscape, street character, transportation, vegetation, local objects, or cultural details that naturally belong to the destination.

Create ONE unified scene rather than a collection of separate elements.

COMPOSITION:
Use an elegant vertical editorial composition with one dominant focal point and several smaller supporting details. Establish clear foreground, middle ground, and background layers using watercolor washes and simplified shapes.

Leave generous warm cream space around important forms. Keep the silhouette clean and immediately recognizable. Avoid overcrowding.

LOCAL STORY:
Show an authentic everyday moment connected to the destination. Include subtle human activity only when it strengthens the story: walking, cycling, sitting, shopping, traveling, eating, working, or simply enjoying the surroundings.

Favor ordinary local atmosphere over generic tourism imagery.

LIGHT & ATMOSPHERE:
Automatically choose lighting that suits the destination and scene: soft morning light, warm afternoon glow, misty weather, gentle sunset, or quiet evening illumination.

Use atmospheric watercolor washes to create depth while maintaining a calm, delicate feeling.

COLOR LANGUAGE:
Build the palette naturally from [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT]. Use warm cream, muted ochre, terracotta, dusty blue, soft green, faded red, warm grey, and subtle golden tones where appropriate.

Keep the colors slightly desaturated, harmonious, and naturally layered.

TYPOGRAPHY:
At the bottom of the artwork, add three restrained editorial text elements:

[LOCATION NAME]
[SHORT DESTINATION-INSPIRED SUBTITLE]
[SHORT WARM POETIC SENTENCE]

Use elegant minimal typography with generous spacing. Keep it secondary to the artwork and ensure all wording is clean and correctly spelled.

FINAL AESTHETIC:
Premium handmade watercolor travel poster × contemporary editorial illustration × nostalgic travel memory × quiet everyday life × sophisticated art-book design.

The finished artwork should feel like a beautifully remembered place painted by hand: atmospheric, personal, refined, understated, and unmistakably connected to [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT].

AVOID:
Any editing workflow, source material, references, existing compositions, copied imagery, collage construction, unrelated landmarks, generic scenery, excessive detail, oversaturated colors, harsh outlines, glossy digital effects, CGI, 3D objects, cartoon characters, clutter, excessive typography, logos, watermarks, interface elements.

FORMAT:
4:5 vertical portrait composition, warm cream paper, handcrafted watercolor texture, generous negative space, premium print-quality finish.

Prompt:
Premium Editorial Poster Instructions
Each uploaded photo must be transformed into a separate, independent premium editorial poster. Never combine multiple photos into one design. Use a strict 3:4 vertical canvas divided horizontally at the exact center into two equal halves, each occupying 50% of the total height and full width, without altering proportions.

The upper half must use the original photo directly without regeneration. Preserve the main subject's identity, human anatomy or architectural structure, proportions, perspective, spatial relationships, textures, natural lighting, shadows, colors, and environment exactly as shown. Only slight cropping and restrained premium color grading are permitted. Do not redraw the main subject, introduce artificial lighting, apply excessive HDR or saturation, create plastic textures, or add fictional elements. If necessary, extend only environmental areas such as the sky, water, ground, walls, plants, or background.

The lower half must reconstruct the photo's central narrative, whether it is a single primary subject or a connected group of elements representing the image's identity, scale, action, or story. Preserve realistic appearance, recognizable identity, proportions, internal structure, texture, and relative positioning. Do not remove important related elements or use a rectangular photo cutout. The reconstructed subject should occupy approximately 55%–80% of the lower half's width. Extend the subject naturally according to the scene's direction, maintaining believable ground contact, waterlines, realistic shadows, or softly fading edges. Integrate it seamlessly into the background without a sticker-like or floating appearance.

Place one narrow, low-saturation geometric color field behind or partially through the subject, creating a subtle transition between photographic realism and editorial abstraction. Extract the color from the original photo and choose a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal orientation according to the scene's narrative direction. The subject must visibly cross the color field's boundary, with part overlapping the colored area and another part extending into the open negative space. Create natural occlusion, overlap, and spatial depth. The color field must not act as a frame or card and must never completely enclose the subject. Use only one primary geometric window. Do not add multiple color blocks, thick borders, rounded corners, strong gradients, or drop shadows.

Use a white, cool-white, very light gray, or near-white background in the lower half, coordinated with the original photograph. Maintain a restrained asymmetrical composition with generous negative space and a clear visual hierarchy: the reconstructed subject as the primary focus, the low-saturation geometric window as the secondary element, and the clean background as supporting space.

The final poster must look premium, refined, realistic, and editorial while preserving the original photo's visual identity, exact two-half composition, original proportions, and overall artistic direction.

Prompt:
Sophisticated contemporary oil portrait painting with expressive, loose brushwork, combining refined semi-realistic portraiture, classical fine-art painting, and modern editorial painterly aesthetics. The subject is rendered with highly controlled yet visibly handcrafted oil strokes, layered pigments, soft impasto, delicate dry-brush marks, and expressive directional brushwork that follows the natural anatomy and volume of the face.

Facial features are detailed and semi-realistic, with luminous skin, natural texture, expressive eyes, carefully modeled nose and lips, and richly layered hair built from flowing individual brushstrokes. Use warm brown, deep umber, burnt sienna, ochre, muted peach, cream, ivory, soft gray-blue, charcoal, and subtle muted gold accents, matching the reference palette precisely. Highlights are predominantly warm ivory and creamy white, while shadows remain deep but soft and painterly.

The background uses the same desaturated blue-gray and warm ivory palette, appearing like an unfinished classical painted canvas. Broad vertical and horizontal brushstrokes, translucent paint layers, softly scraped areas, subtle dry-brush textures, and irregular painterly patches create an atmospheric studio-like backdrop. Keep the background simple, quiet, and organically integrated with the portrait rather than sharply separated.

The lower portion of the figure intentionally becomes unfinished and gradually dissolves into loose white and ivory brushstrokes. Clothing, shoulders, chest, and lower contours progressively lose definition, breaking into scattered semi-transparent strokes and fading pigment. Edges become incomplete, soft, irregular, and partially disappear into the background, creating the unmistakable impression of an intentionally unfinished oil painting. Do not create a hard bottom edge.

Maintain a refined balance between highly detailed facial realism and deliberately unfinished painterly abstraction. Visible brushwork, layered oil pigments, soft impasto, subtle canvas texture, natural imperfections, elegant tonal transitions, museum-quality portrait painting, cinematic atmosphere, timeless fine-art character.

NEGATIVE PROMPT: No photorealistic photography, no 3D CGI, no vector appearance, no hard digital outlines, no glossy rendering, no completely finished lower body, no sharp background separation.

Prompt: 1/2
Using my uploaded photo as the primary facial reference, transform me into an outrageously exaggerated, hyper-realistic, classic children’s TV puppet-inspired trash-can creature while keeping my identity and recognizable facial features unmistakably intact.

CHARACTER DESIGN: Enormous head, tiny upper body, narrow shoulders, short, skinny puppet-like arms, huge expressive eyes, heavy downward-slanting brown eyebrows, long bulbous green nose, and a pronounced grouchy frown. Cover my entire visible head, face, eyebrows, neck, and exposed upper body in vibrant, thick, shaggy green fur with individually defined strands, wild spiky tufts, unruly hair, and tactile, messy texture. Preserve my underlying facial structure and recognizable identity. Expression: comically irritated, judgmental, sarcastic, mischievous, and lovable—not frightening or monstrous. Slightly hunch my shoulders and lean my oversized head forward as if preparing a hilarious sarcastic one-liner.

TRASH CAN AND ANATOMY: My upper torso, shoulders, and arms emerge directly from a classic, battered, open-topped cylindrical galvanized-steel trash can with a thick rolled rim. My entire lower body remains concealed inside. The can is upright, intact, separate from my body, and firmly resting directly on the sidewalk. Show its complete structure from rim to bottom base, including realistic dents, scratches, worn edges, subtle rust, metallic reflections, and a clear contact shadow. Absolutely no visible legs, feet, shoes, or body parts beneath, through, or outside the can. I am sitting inside it, not wearing it as a costume. No floating, hovering, sinking, or hidden visible limb support.

ENVIRONMENT: A richly detailed residential neighborhood at nighttime on Halloween. Include charming suburban houses, glowing jack-o’-lanterns along the sidewalk and on porches, spooky decorations, artificial cobwebs, skeletons, bare tree branches, scattered autumn leaves, warm orange window and porch lights, purple and orange string lights, distant trick-or-treater silhouettes, and subtle drifting nighttime mist. Deep midnight-blue sky, soft moonlight, balanced warm pumpkin illumination and cool blue ambient lighting. Festive, quaint, whimsical, playfully spooky—not genuine horror. Keep the background softly focused and subordinate to my face.

COMPOSITION: Vertical 2:3 portrait, three-quarter camera angle, slightly low perspective. Show the complete trash can from its upper rim to its fully grounded base, my entire visible upper body, oversized head, face, shoulders, and visible arms without cropping. Position the can prominently in the lower and central frame, with my expressive face as the primary focal point. Maintain a strong silhouette, clear separation between green fur, metal rim, and dark background, and enough surrounding scenery to establish the Halloween neighborhood.

RENDERING: Premium cinematic CGI combining practical puppet craftsmanship with photorealistic 3D character artistry. Extraordinary tactile fur detail, layered shaggy eyebrows, realistic eye reflections, convincing facial and mouth anatomy, physically accurate weathered metal, and natural material textures. Use cinematic moonlight, warm pumpkin glow, subtle purple accents, global illumination, physically based materials, ambient occlusion, volumetric mist, delicate rim lighting, realistic contact shadows, and cinematic depth of field. Sharp facial details; softly blurred background.

In the middle a market square with a fountain, striped market stalls and a festival procession; a harbour with a stone quay, wooden crates, nets, fishing boats, a ferry and sailing boats; a lighthouse on a headland; steep terraced hillsides with lemon and olive groves, stone walls and stairways; a hilltop temple and a bell tower; hot-spring baths with steam; windmills; a cable car; a long beach with striped umbrellas and bathers; narrow lanes with washing lines, cafes with awnings, rooftop gardens, a small railway with a train and a stone bridge; a small volcano at the back and a few islets with palm trees. About 200 minuscule people, each doing something: dancers and drummers in the procession, market sellers, fishermen mending nets, bathers, hikers, cafe guests, kids running, a bride and groom. A standing person is only about 3% of the picture height.

The look is the point: slightly wobbly black pen outlines with a flat, matte gouache colour fill, a bright cheerful limited palette (turquoise sea, terracotta roofs, olive green, lemon yellow, coral, cream), tiny flat cast shadows, small stylised waves drawn as short curved lines, aged cream paper texture with faint creases. Hand-drawn, not a photograph, not 3D, no blurred painting. The drawing fills the whole picture to all four edges: no frame, no border, no title banner, no compass rose, no scale bar, no legend, no map pins.

Exactly one small logo: a small black hanging signboard in front of a cafe in the right half, about 4% of the picture width, with a white paw print whose big pad holds a swirling ocean wave, and the word "Shoji" in white cursive brush lettering to its right. Apart from that sign there are no letters, words or numbers anywhere: no place names, labels or signs with writing.

THE ONLY ANIMALS IN THE WHOLE PICTURE ARE FOUR CATS, and there are never more than four. Not five, not a spare one. No other animal at all: no whales, dolphins, fish, seagulls or other birds, no horses, donkeys, goats, sheep, dogs, chickens, no animal-shaped boats, signs, weathervanes or statues. No person wears an animal head or costume. The four cats are tiny, in the same middle band of the picture, each in the open and never hidden behind anything, none in the lower third. The three real cats are each only about 1.5% of the picture height, under half the height of a standing person, and wear a thin red collar with a tiny gold bell:
1. a black-and-white "hachiware" cat (black head and back, a white blaze splitting the face, white chest and paws) sitting upright on the stone quay beside a pile of wooden crates, in the left half;
2. a brown mackerel tabby (warm brown fur with dark stripes, white muzzle and chest) sitting upright on a low stone terrace wall among lemon trees, upper left;
3. a calico cat (white with orange and black patches) sitting on the steps at the foot of a striped market stall, right of centre;
4. Shoji Cat, an upright orange tabby cat about three heads tall in a black leather jacket, denim shorts, cream sneakers and black wayfarer sunglasses with blue and red lenses, dancing with one arm raised in the festival procession in the middle of the market square, about one and a half times as tall as each of the other three cats.
No dark round objects or dark animal-like shapes that could be mistaken for a cat. No watermark.

BOTTOM TRAVEL COLLAGE

- A die-cut travel sticker depicting an iconic national landmark.

Finish with a circular "MADE IN {{COUNTRY}}" stamp, miniature national-symbol postage stamp, tiny airplane with a dashed flight path, and the national motto in small italic lettering.

Use restrained national flag colors, realistic paper fibers, distressed ink, hand-painted illustrations, natural contact shadows, soft studio lighting, and slightly desaturated vintage colors. Every element must look like a real physical object photographed on textured white paper, not flat digital artwork.

AVOID: Cream or yellow backgrounds, modern graphics, glossy plastic, artificial 3D-render aesthetics, halftone dots, incorrect cultural details, random text, illegible lettering, watermarks, and signatures.

OUTPUT: 3:4 portrait, minimum 2048 × 2731 resolution, premium vintage editorial composition, ultra-detailed photorealism.

A handsome male model walks confidently forward in a sophisticated, layered menswear ensemble, captured from a straight-on, chest-level perspective. His hair is a medium-length layered cut—shorter on the sides with three to four inches on top reaching his eyebrows—styled with a wet-look pomade that enhances its natural texture, featuring slight frizz and uneven clumping. A deep, off-center right part creates a deliberately disheveled look, allowing several loose, wavy S-curl strands to fall naturally across his forehead and right brow. His facial expression is composed and posed, with a closed neutral mouth, relaxed eyebrows, and a direct gaze framed by round tortoiseshell glasses. He wears a crisp white dress shirt with a visible collar and cuffs, paired with a brown tie and a chocolate dark espresso brown long-sleeve knit polo sweater featuring a buttoned placket. His lower half consists of dark brown double-pleated high-waisted trousers held by a cognac leather brown belt with a silver buckle, ending in black leather loafers. His left hand is tucked completely into his left front trouser pocket, pulling the fabric to create a subtle tension, while his right arm rests by his side, the hand securely gripping the dual leather handles of a large cognac brown leather tote bag with knuckles moderately visible. He strides across a foreground of worn, light gray-beige smooth concrete paving stones that bear subtle stains and natural texturing, grounding the scene in an authentic outdoor urban street setting. Behind him, the midground opens up into a slightly blurred, medium-depth classic European street featuring a warm stone beige limestone building facade. This pristine yet historically weathered ashlar masonry displays matte textures, horizontal block joints, and classical pilasters with structural reveals. To the mid-height right, a vintage black wrought-iron window balcony railing catches the eye with ornate gold and brass medallion detailing, beautifully contrasting the pale stone. The atmosphere evokes an elegant, quiet urban morning wrapped in a sophisticated monochromatic brown and neutral palette, illuminated by a single, large diffused source of open-sky daylight pouring in from above and slightly front-left. This soft, moderate-intensity outdoor light casts neutral ambient fill and short, gray shadows with soft gradual edges on the pavement beneath him, as well as subtle shading under his chin and the leather bag. Radiant, preserved specular highlights gently touch his forehead, the tip of his nose, the top curves of the leather tote bag, and the polished shoe leather, creating a dynamic, high-contrast visual hierarchy that draws the eye from his well-lit face down through the dark textures of his outfit. Rendered as tack-sharp digital photography reminiscent of high-end luxury menswear lookbooks and classic sartorial street style, the image utilizes an 85mm lens at f/2.8 with a 1/500s shutter speed to freeze motion while maintaining a crisp subject against the softened architectural backdrop, finalized with subtle warm color grading and selective clarity to enhance the intricate knitwear and leather textures, all beautifully framed in a 4:5 aspect ratio.

Prompt:
Create an exceptionally beautiful, sophisticated 3D paper-quilling architectural artwork featuring [LANDMARK NAME], [CITY], [COUNTRY], inspired by the reference image.

1. CENTRAL LANDMARK

Feature one iconic landmark as the dominant subject.
Preserve its authentic architectural silhouette and recognisable details.
Recreate the architecture using intricate rolled-paper strips, delicate paper coils and carefully arranged quilled shapes.
Give the structure beautiful raised, sculptural dimensions.
Make the landmark appear handcrafted from individually shaped and assembled paper.

2. MINIMALIST GEOMETRIC LANDSCAPE

Surround the landmark with a simple, elegant abstract landscape.

Large circular sun or moon behind the architecture.
Layered geometric mountains and hills.
Simple curved foreground shapes.
Minimal architectural platforms or steps.
Clean overlapping paper layers.
No unnecessary decorative elements.

Keep the landscape flat and geometric while making the landmark richly detailed through paper quilling.

3. SIGNATURE PAPER-QUILLING TECHNIQUE

This is the defining feature.

Intricately rolled and curled paper strips.
Fine spiral coils and delicate loops.
Precisely arranged parallel paper lines.
Raised paper edges and visible thickness.
Beautifully sculpted architectural curves.
Realistic miniature paper craftsmanship.
Subtle natural shadows between individual paper pieces.

The quilling should be most detailed on the landmark, while the surrounding landscape remains clean and minimal.

4. UNIQUE COLOUR IDENTITY

Choose a completely different colour palette for every destination.

Use 4–6 coordinated colours inspired by the landmark’s architecture, culture and surroundings.

Change the colours of:

Landmark paper coils.
Background sun.
Geometric mountains.
Foreground landscape.
Supporting paper details.

Avoid repeating colour combinations across destinations.

5. PRESENTATION AND LAYOUT

Square or near-square central artwork.
Soft, pale neutral background.
Generous white space around the composition.
Elegant white mounting paper.
Deep navy or destination-inspired contrasting outer mat.
Realistic soft shadows.
Professional gallery-style presentation.
Front-facing, perfectly balanced composition.

6. HANDWRITTEN TYPOGRAPHY

Write the actual landmark name beneath the artwork.

[LANDMARK NAME]

Use a beautiful, natural handwritten script font, as though the name has been personally written by an artist with a fine calligraphy pen.

Keep the lettering elegant, slightly flowing and artistic.

Do not use bold block letters or mechanical typography.

7. FINAL ART DIRECTION

Premium handmade paper-quilling artwork, minimalist architectural illustration, geometric landscape design, intricate paper sculpture, tactile cardstock texture and sophisticated gallery presentation.

The result should look like a real handcrafted paper artwork photographed in a professional art studio.

No photographic architecture, no plastic 3D appearance, no flowers, no unnecessary leaves, no watermark, no extra text.

Vertical 3:4 aspect ratio. Full-bleed premium editorial poster. Exactly 50% authentic photographic scene on top and 50% matching black-and-white hand-drawn screen-print illustration on the bottom.

Use the uploaded reference photograph directly in the upper 50% of the poster.

Preserve its original photographic quality, sharpness, natural lighting, and color relationships.

Allow only subtle, intelligent cropping around the outer edges when necessary, without compromising the main subject.

If required, naturally extend a small portion of the surrounding environment to fit the composition.

Do not redraw, illustrate, stretch, blur, or modify the subject's appearance, structure, or spatial relationships.

Do not introduce black borders, white margins, or empty edges.

2. BOTTOM HALF — MINIMALIST EDITORIAL ILLUSTRATION

Use a warm, near-white ivory paper background with an extremely subtle paper texture.

Analyze the main subject and visual story of the uploaded reference image.

Extract only the primary subject, preserving one or two essential identifying elements.

Remove or heavily simplify all secondary details, including background architecture, crowds, vehicles, fences, signs, trees, and other unnecessary elements.

Transform the primary subject into a sophisticated black-ink editorial illustration.

ILLUSTRATION STYLE:

Use natural, clean pen strokes with varied line weight.

Preserve an authentic hand-drawn appearance with expressive but controlled linework.

Avoid overly precise engraving aesthetics, excessive internal details, and dense cross-hatching.

Place a large, nearly pure-black rectangular ink block behind the illustrated subject.

The rectangular block should have subtly imperfect, handmade print-style edges.

Keep the black background clean, with only fine paper grain and minimal noise.

Avoid obvious hatching, scratches, architectural lines, or complex textures.

ILLUSTRATION SCALE AND COMPOSITION:

The illustrated subject must occupy approximately 72–77% of the canvas width and 58–64% of the bottom section's height.

Maintain a clear visual focal point with generous negative space surrounding the illustration.

3. COLOR RULES

The bottom illustration must follow a strictly black-and-white color palette by default.

Preserve only one localized accent color if the original reference image contains a clearly distinctive, concentrated color element with meaningful narrative importance.

Ordinary blue skies, green vegetation, stone surfaces, skin tones, and environmental colors must not be treated as accent colors.

Any preserved accent color must remain strictly localized to the relevant subject or area.

Never allow accent colors to spread across the entire illustration.

4. TYPOGRAPHY AND EDITORIAL LAYOUT

Automatically generate concise, meaningful English typography based on the content of the uploaded reference photograph.

The typography must resemble handwritten editorial annotations from an independent art publication.

TOP-LEFT CORNER:

Generate a short handwritten title consisting of 2–5 words, arranged across two lines.

Directly beneath the title, include three short English action verbs relevant to the photograph.

TOP-RIGHT CORNER:

Display only two lines of geographic coordinates:

Latitude
Longitude

Do not include any additional text in this area.

BOTTOM-LEFT CORNER:

Display the location name followed by the word "DIARY."

Directly beneath it, add one short descriptive English sentence inspired by the photograph.

TYPOGRAPHY STYLE:

Use a rough, upright, slightly irregular handwritten typeface.

Maintain subtle imperfections and a natural editorial annotation aesthetic.

Avoid elegant cursive, calligraphy, overly decorative lettering, and excessively polished typography.

5. FINAL ART DIRECTION

The finished poster must combine:

Authentic, high-quality photography.
Minimalist black-and-white editorial illustration.
Generous negative space.
Independent art publication aesthetics.
Quiet, restrained, sophisticated visual storytelling.
Natural handwritten typography.
A balanced relationship between documentary realism and expressive hand-drawn artwork.

The overall result should resemble a carefully designed, collectible editorial art print.

6. FINAL OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS

ASPECT RATIO:
2:3 vertical.

RESOLUTION:
High-resolution, sharp, print-quality output.

COMPOSITION:

Exactly 50% original reference photography on top.

Exactly 50% editorial illustration on the bottom.

One perfectly straight horizontal dividing line.

One complete, standalone poster.

RESTRICTIONS:

No collages.
No multi-poster layouts.
No combined images.
No unnecessary decorative elements.
No modifications to the original subject's identity or appearance.
No excessive illustration details.
No changes to the original photograph's natural color relationships.

FINAL GOAL:

Create a sophisticated, visually balanced editorial art poster that faithfully preserves the uploaded reference photograph while transforming its primary subject into an expressive, minimalist black-ink illustration.

Display the destination name prominently across the top in oversized, bold, geometric uppercase lettering. Typography should feel artistic, distinctive and inspired by the visual identity of the location.

3. Cultural symbols and illustrations

Incorporate 3–5 simplified graphic elements that genuinely represent the selected destination, such as:

* Recognizable architectural landmarks.
* Traditional cultural symbols, patterns or motifs.
* Local plants, flowers, animals or natural elements.
* Famous mountains, rivers, deserts or coastlines.
* Historic objects, decorative symbols or regional art forms.

Arrange these elements as separate artistic compositions rather than realistic scenes.

4. Landscape illustration

Use simplified geometric mountain ranges, architectural silhouettes, rolling hills, desert dunes, coastlines or other location-specific landscapes.

Include a small silhouette of a locally relevant animal, tree or other distinctive element in the foreground where appropriate.

5. Graphic style

* Flat vector-style illustrations.
* Bold geometric shapes and clean outlines.
* Abstract symbolic artwork.
* Strong negative space.
* Minimalist silhouettes.
* Smooth curves and angular patterns.
* Subtle vintage print texture.
* No photorealism or 3D effects.

6. Unique colour identity

IMPORTANT: Select a completely different, destination-inspired colour palette for every new poster.

Do not automatically reuse the same colours. Choose 3–5 harmonious colours inspired by the location’s natural landscape, architecture, cultural heritage, traditional textiles or regional identity.

Use one dominant background colour, one contrasting illustration colour, one accent colour and a warm neutral for secondary details.

Premium collectible travel-art poster, vertical 2:3 format, balanced composition, bold typography, sophisticated colour blocking, clean geometric illustrations and timeless vintage graphic-design aesthetics.

Important: Make every poster visually unique while maintaining the same overall design language. Use authentic destination-specific symbols, accurate local script where appropriate, and correctly spelled destination names. Avoid generic decorative symbols that do not belong to the selected location.

GPT image 2.5 prompt share

Try it with prompt : ADIDAS RUNNING — “RUN IT BACK”

FORMAT: 4:5 vertical | Premium social media advertising | Retro editorial design

CREATIVE DIRECTION

Act as a senior advertising art director and editorial graphic designer developing an original retro-inspired adidas Running campaign. Combine the visual energy of 1990s sports magazines, vintage sneaker advertising, experimental typography, and contemporary commercial art direction.

The result must feel like a thoughtfully designed print campaign rediscovered from an archival sports magazine—not a generic vintage filter applied to a modern poster.

BRAND & PRODUCT LOCK

Hero product: adidas running shoe, using the supplied product reference as the source of truth.

Preserve the actual silhouette, proportions, outsole geometry, upper construction, lacing, materials, colorway, Three Stripes placement, adidas branding, and other identifiable product details. Do not invent a new shoe or redesign existing branding.

VISUAL STYLE SYSTEM

Bold 1990s sports-editorial design with oversized condensed typography, asymmetrical graphic blocks, photographic cutouts, visible print grain, halftone textures, and layered magazine-inspired compositions.

Use intentional imperfections while keeping the advertising polished, legible, and commercially credible.

COMPOSITION & LAYOUT

Create a strong, immediately recognizable hero composition.

The sneaker and/or runner must dominate the visual hierarchy. Use oversized cropped typography as a structural design element, not merely a caption. Introduce contrasting geometric color panels, small editorial annotations, and carefully controlled negative space.

Every element must have a defined role. Avoid arbitrary decoration.

TYPOGRAPHIC SYSTEM

Primary headline: “RUN IT BACK”

Use bold, condensed, high-impact display typography. Allow deliberate cropping and close letter spacing where appropriate. Add restrained secondary copy in small editorial text blocks.

Preserve the exact spelling of supplied copy. Do not generate fake prices, awards, technical claims, or product specifications.

COLOR SYSTEM

Vintage red: #D62820
Cobalt blue: #2448A5
Warm cream: #EDE4D1
Deep black: #171717
Accent orange: #F16A45

Use cream as a paper-inspired base, red for dominant emphasis, cobalt for contrasting graphic blocks, and black for typography and detail. Orange is a restrained accent.

PHOTOGRAPHY & LIGHTING

Use authentic sports-editorial photography, believable athletic anatomy, natural movement, directional light, realistic contact shadows, and tactile material detail.

Add subtle analog film grain and print texture without obscuring the shoe’s construction or branding. Avoid excessive sharpening, synthetic plastic surfaces, and artificial HDR effects.

GRAPHIC DETAILS

Incorporate restrained halftone patterns, small catalog-style annotations, hand-drawn directional marks, cutout photography, and occasional sticker-like graphic shapes.

Keep these elements subordinate to the hero product and headline. Maintain deliberate alignment and visual rhythm.

OUTPUT

4:5 vertical composition for an Instagram feed campaign. High-resolution commercial finish with clear hierarchy, intentional edge cropping, controlled detail, and consistent adidas brand presentation.

EXCLUSIONS & QUALITY CONTROL

No incorrect sneaker silhouette, duplicated Three Stripes, malformed adidas logos, invented product details, distorted anatomy, illegible headline, random text, excessive grunge, cluttered composition, generic 3D-render appearance, or watermarks.

Final quality standard: a distinctive, art-directed sports advertisement with a coherent retro design system, accurate product representation, and professional social-media campaign execution.

GPT Image 2.5

Prompt:
Create a premium 3:4 vertical editorial travel-memory poster for [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT].

TEXT-TO-IMAGE ONLY — generate the entire artwork creatively from [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT] alone. No reference image required.

COMPOSITION
Divide the poster into two perfectly equal horizontal halves with no gap.

TOP HALF — CINEMATIC PHOTOGRAPH
Create a wide horizontal, photorealistic travel photograph representing [COUNTRY / CITY / LOCATION / SUBJECT]. Automatically choose the most meaningful subject, architecture, landscape, or moment associated with the destination.

The image must feel like an authentic editorial photograph: natural perspective, realistic lighting, subtle color grading, strong central subject, cinematic atmosphere, and believable environmental details.

BOTTOM HALF — OPEN-BOOK JOURNAL
Create one fully opened horizontal hardcover photography book centered in the lower half, viewed almost from above with slight realistic perspective.

The book should occupy roughly 86% of the lower-half width. The spine must sit exactly in the center, with perfectly equal left and right pages. Show realistic paper edges, thickness, spine curvature, soft shadows, and premium tactile paper.

LEFT PAGE
Fill the entire left page with one dominant color naturally extracted from the destination’s visual identity.

Place a smaller horizontal landscape photograph at the center of the page, showing the same destination or subject from the upper scene. Keep it rectangular, clean, and surrounded by an even generous border.

RIGHT PAGE
Use warm ivory paper with abundant negative space.

At the upper center, add one elegant 3–5 word ALL-CAPS English title inspired by the mood of the destination. Use small black typewriter-style serif lettering with subtle letter spacing.

Below it, place ONE perfectly upright vintage vertical postage stamp. Give it a cream perforated border, subtle paper texture, and a delicate shadow.

Inside the stamp, do not simply reproduce the main photograph. Instead, reinterpret 2–4 recognizable elements from the destination as a playful editorial illustration using bold hand-drawn black outlines, simplified shapes, and ONE bright accent color drawn from the scene.

Below the stamp, add two short centered lines of gentle poetic English text.

BACKGROUND
Outside the open book, create a softly blurred continuation of the destination’s environment. Preserve only its general colors, light, and atmosphere while keeping individual objects indistinct.

STYLE
Cinematic travel photography × contemporary photography monograph × open-book visual diary × vintage postage illustration × minimalist editorial design.

Warm, quiet, sophisticated, tactile, intimate, and collectible.

PRIORITIES
Perfect 50/50 top-bottom division → perfectly centered book spine → equal pages → strong horizontal photography → intact upright stamp → generous negative space.

Avoid portrait-oriented photo panels, blurred side bars, stretched imagery, invented landmarks, distorted architecture, uneven pages, tilted or cropped books, multiple stamps, excessive decoration, clutter, logos, watermarks, UI elements, or unnecessary typography.

FORMAT
3:4 vertical, two equal halves, premium editorial photography, realistic open-book construction, refined typography, cohesive travel-journal aesthetic.

Prompt 👇

A realistic, straight-on, eye-level medium-full street fashion editorial portrait captures a young man from the thighs up, centrally positioned and caught mid-stride with his weight shifted forward onto his left leg, his body angled fifteen degrees to the right with level, relaxed shoulders. He features medium-length wavy light brown hair styled in a center part with curtain bangs extending to his cheekbones and nape, showcasing natural textured layers with slight flyaways held back by rectangular sunglasses resting on top of his head. His expression is calm, focused, and aloof in a posed candid manner, with relaxed neutral eyebrows, lowered eyelids gazing down at his coffee cup, and a closed, neutral mouth with relaxed lips. He is dressed in a sophisticated layered winter ensemble consisting of a jet-black turtleneck underneath a dark espresso brown leather collared shirt, topped with a cropped brown suede bomber jacket and paired with wide-leg black trousers. Both of his hands are clad in cool slate-gray leather gloves and raised to chest level with natural, functional tension; his right hand wraps firmly around the middle of a black disposable coffee cup featuring a subtle, partial bold modern sans-serif white logo while his right arm pins a new, folded white newspaper displaying regular editorial serif black text and a small visible image tightly against his ribs, and his left hand hovers with fingers curled lightly near the coffee lid as if about to adjust or open it. He walks along an outdoor European city street in winter, stepping across a dark charcoal-gray stone sidewalk and asphalt street covered in irregular patches of melting white snow, slush, and tire and foot tracks. In the bottom left midground, the rear bumper of a used black sedan is partially visible, showing dark paint, a red taillight, and a partial white license plate ending in the numbers 88. Directly behind him, a clean, well-maintained classic European building facade balances the symmetric composition, featuring a matte, rough-grained off-white stucco plaster wall with cool gray undertones, uniform color variation, carved horizontal and arched faux stone block grooves, decorative keystones above the arches, and a small metal basement grate on the lower left. Within the facade, the center and left background showcase medium-sized arched stone window frames fitted with pulled-down light gray horizontal slatted metal roller shutters, while the right background is dominated by a well-maintained vintage arched double entrance door crafted from warm medium-brown stained wood with four vertical rectangular glass panels in the upper section and an arched transom window above. The chilly, curated urban morning atmosphere is illuminated by moderate, soft, diffused natural overcast daylight from a single overhead sky source, supplemented by natural ambient bounce fill reflecting off the white building and snow. This cool-toned lighting creates a flat, low-contrast ratio with short, soft-edged gray shadows tucked under his chin, beneath the jacket folds, and slightly under the architectural ledges, alongside subtle highlights catching on his cheekbones, nose bridge, leather gloves, and snow patches. The color profile relies on a desaturated, medium-contrast palette of neutral earth tones and monochromatic darks, blending the off-white stucco, jet black, dark espresso brown, warm wood brown, and cool slate gray. Captured as tack-sharp digital photography using a 35mm or 50mm lens at f/4.0, 1/250s, and ISO 200 with a natural overcast white balance and deep depth of field that keeps both the subject and the architectural background in clear focus without any grain, the clean visual style channel influences of European menswear street style, old money aesthetics, and contemporary social media fashion, finished with post-processing that applies slight background desaturation, rich contrast in the blacks and browns, and a cool winter tone curve, all framed in a 2:3 aspect ratio.
